faults.quote: The network is the same six routes as in FY2023, with the same number of flights on each. Here's an exhibit: Larkspur Air — Results by route, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($ millions unless noted).
faults.why: The candidate asked for departures and average fare. Flights are covered, but average fare gets no word: no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: On Hub–Port Avery, revenue fell from $46.8M to $32.4M and contribution fell from $13.8M to a $0.6M loss, on 3,000 flights a year.
faults.why: This repeats an Exhibit 1 line that is already on screen. The candidate asked only for Port Avery's FY2023 fare.

faults.quote: I'm putting up an exhibit: Hub–Lakeport — Economics of one one-way flight, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($).
faults.why: The candidate also asked when the fare started dropping. That part gets no word this turn; the timing only arrives with competitor_entry at t10.

faults.quote: Earlier you said Lakeport was around $160 in FY2023 after applying a 33% decline to $120. Which base did you apply the 33% to?
faults.why: At t9 the candidate had already replaced the $160 estimate with the exhibit's actual $200 FY2023 fare and its 40% drop.

faults.quote: Variable cost on the new routes is estimated at $9,200 per flight, across 5,000 flights a year that would use the aircraft time freed by exiting Hub–Lakeport (2,000 flights) and Hub–Port Avery (3,000 flights).
faults.why: The candidate asked only about the entrant's cost and schedule. This releases new-route data nobody asked for, and it hands over the exit-and-redeploy solution well before that stage.

faults.quote: The low-cost airline's cost per seat is about 30% lower than Larkspur's — it flies larger planes and has lower labor costs — and its fares are about the same as Larkspur's current fares.
faults.why: The candidate also asked how many flights a day the entrant runs. That part gets no word and no 'I don't have'.

faults.quote: Walk me through how you got that figure and why Port Avery's fare erosion is the right number to apply to Lakeport.
faults.why: The $4,800 per flight of lost revenue is correct: Lakeport's own fare drop is also $80 × 60 passengers. Challenging correct math is a fault.

faults.quote: Walk me through how you got that figure
faults.why: 'That figure' dangles, with no clear referent named.

faults.quote: Air travel demand in Larkspur's cities has been roughly flat.
faults.why: The candidate asked for a demand estimate for the new candidate routes. This line covers demand in Larkspur's existing cities.

faults.quote: New routes typically take 6–12 months to reach their expected load factor, and in the first year the load factor is often around 60%. What do those figures tell you?
faults.why: At t17 the candidate applied the entrant's 30% cost-per-seat gap to the $20M fixed cost base, claiming $6M addressable and $13.8M profit. Leases are locked through 2030. This was never probed or corrected.
